name: Nantosuelta
text: Nantosuelta, also written Nantosvelta, is a Gaulish goddess of the raven whose cult is attested at several sites, Britain among them. Her images puzzle interpreters. One hand holds a saucer or patera, evidently for sacrifice on an altar, and in some images a small pot takes its place, perhaps recalling the great Celtic cauldron. Her other hand bears what seems to be a small house at the tip of a long pole. The patera and the house-on-pole suggest prosperity, well-being, and domestic life, while her steady company of the carrion-eating raven speaks of death. Her usual cult partner is Sucellus, whose name means the good striker.

attributes.attribute: Gaulish raven-goddess worshipped in Gaul and Britain

key_results: Nantosuelta is a Gaulish raven-goddess with sites in Britain too.
Her icons pair a patera or pot with a house on a long pole.
Sucellus, the good striker, is her usual cult partner.
